candidate.title: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
candidate.abstract: Autonomous AI research agents aim to accelerate scientific discovery by automating the research pipeline, from hypothesis generation to peer review. However, existing benchmarks rarely test a fundamental bottleneck: whether Large Language Models can judge the methodological viability of a research idea before expending time and computational resources. We introduce SoundnessBench, a curated benchmark of 1,099 machine-learning research proposals reconstructed from ICLR submissions, labeled with reviewer soundness sub-scores, and audited against source papers. SoundnessBench should be interpreted as a benchmark for recoverable proposal-stage soundness rather than exact prediction of full-paper review outcomes. Across 12 frontier LLMs, we find a pervasive optimism bias: under standard prompting, models frequently rate low-soundness proposals as sound, while aggressive prompting largely shifts errors from false positives to false negatives. Additional controls for public-corpus contamination, paper-identifying phrases, surface features, and human audit quality suggest that this behavior is not explained by a single confounder. Our results indicate that current LLMs are not yet reliable as standalone first-gate evaluators for scientific rigor.
candidate.authors: Sy-Tuyen Ho, Ming-Hui Liu, H. Nghiem, Furong Huang

extraction.method: 构建研究提案合理性基准，含污染与特征控制
extraction.scenario: LLM评判研究想法方法可行性
extraction.benchmark: 12个前沿LLM，对比审稿人合理性子分数
extraction.results: 普遍存在乐观偏差，标准提示下常将低合理性提案评为合理，激进提示使错误从假阳性转向假阴性
extraction.limitations: 仅评测提案阶段合理性，非完整论文评审结果
extraction.summary: 论文提出SoundnessBench，评测LLM能否判断研究想法的方法可行性。基准含1099个从ICLR投稿重建的ML研究提案，标注审稿人合理性子分数并对照源论文审计。评测12个前沿LLM发现普遍乐观偏差，标准提示下常将低合理性提案评为合理，激进提示则使错误从假阳性转向假阴性，表明当前LLM尚不能作为科研严谨性的独立首关评估者。
